reason: R1 and R0 form a symmetric resistive link between VOUT1 and VOUT2 via net12. If you remove only R1 (keeping R0), the circuit still has a valid DC solution and will amplify, but you lose the intended symmetry and any common-mode/cross-coupling effect that resistor network provides.
impact_estimate: Low-to-moderate: functionality remains, but output balance/CM behavior may shift; remove as a pair if the coupling is non-essential.

reason: M5 appears to generate/bias node net23 (feeding the PMOS current sources M6/M7) from VB2; if net23 is instead driven by an ideal bias source or otherwise held at the correct DC voltage, M5 is redundant. Removing it is safe only if you replace its biasing function externally (e.g., tie net23 to a suitable bias or include a different bias circuit).
impact_estimate: Low if net23 is externally biased; high if not (bias collapses and the input pair/load currents may become incorrect).
